title: 1545-markov-decision-processes-with-dynamic-transition
universal_lens: A Bayesian hierarchical Markov decision process models dynamic shooting strategies in basketball using non-stationary transition probabilities indexed by shot-clock intervals. Markov decision processes unify situational football policy learning via state-transitions, rewards, and counterfactual simulations.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive distributions over MDP policies to estimate team-specific shooting behaviors under temporal covariance structures derived from optical tracking data. The framework implements a GSI-style sequential Bayesian updating pipeline: first-stage conformal predictive intervals for raw tracking data (STATS LLC), second-stage hierarchical posterior draws for player-level latent states (shrinkage parameter ρ̂_θ), yielding empirical Bayes credible intervals for policy alteration effects (e.g., EPPS/EPPP changes).
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes state-transition tensors to simulate play sequences, incorporating shot-clock dynamics and defensive pressure to predict optimal shooting decisions in real-time. GSE's situational reasoning layer can adopt the transition kernel R(·) as a state-transition matrix for discrete-event game simulators, while its state-transition mapping leverages the same posterior draws to propagate uncertainty in ballhandler decisions through branching play trees, though current v5.2.7 lacks native policy-counterfactual capability.

primitives.name: Dynamic Transition Probability Tensor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Non-stationarity handled by transition probability tensors (TPTs): n_TPT = 8 slices, each a transition matrix for a 3-second shot-clock interval (T(c_n) maps clock time to slice 1–8).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'transition probability tensor, dimensionless', 't': 'shot-clock time, seconds', 'n': 'number of discrete court regions, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Transition probabilities vary smoothly with shot-clock time; each slice represents a fixed time interval.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At shot-clock expiry, transitions map to turnover or end-of-play states.

layer2.mapping: The TPT framework mirrors GSE's state-transition kernel, where each time-slice corresponds to a conditional policy update in response to evolving game context.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical transition frequency matrices across shot-clock bins.

primitives.name: Hierarchical Policy Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each MDP component (policy π, transitions P, reward R) estimated with Bayesian hierarchical models in Stan (2 chains, R̂ < 1.05, ESS 48–15,000).

primitives.assumptions: Policy estimates are informed by group-level priors and individual-level likelihoods.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When data sparsity occurs, hierarchical shrinkage stabilizes estimates.

layer2.mapping: The Bayesian estimator provides GSI with uncertainty quantification for policy decisions, enabling robust inference on team performance.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior effective sample size (ESS) and convergence diagnostic (R̂).

primitives.name: Average Chain Theorem
primitives.verbatim_quote: Novel "average chain" theorem: 500+ lineup-specific chains combined into one team-average chain whose expected transition count per state-pair equals the weighted sum of the chains' expected counts (derivation via canonical Q/U absorbing-chain form).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_{ij}': 'expected number of transitions from state i to j, dimensionless', 'w_k': 'weight for lineup k, dimensionless', 'N_{ij}^{(k)}': 'transitions for lineup k, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Lineup-specific chains are independent and identically distributed with known weights.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In cases of low lineup diversity, average chain may underrepresent rare strategic patterns.

layer2.mapping: The average chain theorem enables GSE to aggregate heterogeneous player behavior into a single representative policy trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: Weighted average transition counts across lineups.

primitives.name: Court Region State Space
primitives.verbatim_quote: State = ballcarrier × 6 court regions (rim/paint/mid-range/corner-3/arc-3/backcourt) × defensive pressure (open/contested) — ~180 states/team.

primitives.assumptions: States are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive for each play.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ball carrier is undefined, state representation becomes ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: This structured state space allows GSE to encode contextual features such as shot difficulty and defensive intensity into its decision-making engine.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of state visits per region-pressure combination.

primitives.name: Shrinkage Policy Modeling
primitives.verbatim_quote: Temporal autocorrelation estimate ρ̂_θ = 0.94 (strong smoothing of shot policies).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\pi_{t}(a|s)': 'Probability of action a at state s and time t (dimensionless)', '\\bar{\\pi}': 'League-average policy (dimensionless)', '\\pi^{(\\text{local})}_{t}(a|s)': 'Local empirical policy (dimensionless)', '\\rho_{\\theta}': 'Temporal autocorrelation coefficient (dimensionless, 0 < \\rho_{\\theta} < 1)', '\\alpha': ' Shrinkage weight (dimensionless, 0 \\leq \\alpha \\leq 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Strong temporal stationarity (ρ̂_θ ≈ 1), i.i.d. local policies, Dirichlet conjugate prior, and no systematic offensive adaptation to policy interventions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: α → 1 (no shrinkage) when ρ̂_θ → 1, leading to overfitting on short-term streaks; α → 0 recovers pure league average, eliminating individuality.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's discrete-event state-transition logic where each node represents a ballhandler decision (action a) with learned transition probabilities. The shrinkage term acts as a regularization prior on edge weights, preventing overfitting in sparse branches.
layer2.telemetry: Observed vs. predicted shot frequency discrepancies after intervention (EPPS/EPPP metrics)

primitives.name: Counterfactual Policy Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Policy results (300 sims each, Cavaliers): Alteration 1 (cut contested mid-range 20% with >10s on clock) — no practical EPPS/EPPP change (only 7.5% of plays end in mid-range shots with >10s left).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {"\\pi, \\pi'": 'Base and altered policy functions (dimensionless)', 'R': 'Expected points per possession (dimensionless)', 'P': 'Scoring efficacy (dimensionless)', '\\Delta \\text{EPPS}, \\Delta \\text{EPPP}': 'Absolute change in expected points per shot/system (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Average-chain invariance (rebounders/teammates do not affect ballhandler transitions), no defensive adaptation, and linear additivity of policy impacts across all states.
primitives.breakdown_regime: ΔEPPS/EPPP → 0 when altered action has low marginal frequency (<7.5% in this case) or when the altered region has near-neutral scoring value.

layer2.mapping: Simulates alternative decision paths in GSE's branching tree by reweighting edges according to π' versus π, accumulating leaf-node outcomes to estimate overall win probability deltas.
layer2.telemetry: Historical win-rate comparison between actual game trajectories and simulated altered trajectories

primitives.name: Defense Non-Adversarial Assumption
primitives.verbatim_quote: (2) Defense non-adversarial: policy gains assume no defensive adaptation (authors' Raptors example suggests adaptation is partial, but it's observational).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V^{\\text{obs}}': "Observed value function under altered policy π' (dimensionless)", 'V^{\\text{true}}': 'True value function accounting for full defensive adaptation (dimensionless)', '\\epsilon': 'Observational bias due to static defense (dimensionless)', "\\mathbb{E}[\\cdot | \\pi']": "Conditional expectation given policy π'"}
primitives.assumptions: Defensive systems are exogenous, fixed across seasons, and independent of offensive strategy, violating the closed-loop feedback inherent in real-game adaptation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Bias term ε → 0 only if defenses perfectly randomize or if the sample size of adaptations is infinite, both unrealistic.

layer2.mapping: Derives an adversarial correction factor c(\pi') = \frac{V^{\text{true}}}{V^{\text{obs}}} \approx 1 - \frac{\text{Cov}(\pi', \text{Defense)}}{\text{Var}(V^{\text{obs}})}$ for GSE's minimax tree search, where covariance captures observed adaptation patterns.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in opponent defensive efficiency before vs. after policy shift

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter introduces a unified Bayesian hierarchical MDP framework that integrates three core components: policy (π), scoring efficacy (P), and transition (R) models. The key innovation is using posterior draws from the hierarchical model to simulate counterfactual policies, such as altering shot distributions or pass networks. The temporal autocorrelation ρ̂_θ = 0.94 implies strong persistence in player behavior, justifying aggressive shrinkage toward the league mean. The empirical results demonstrate that small policy changes have minimal impact unless they target high-frequency actions (e.g., Alteration 2 vs. Alteration 1). The 'defense non-adversarial' assumption is a critical limitation, as real defenses will adapt, reducing the observed gains. This work bridges the gap between static shot charts and dynamic decision processes, providing a rigorous probabilistic foundation for strategic analysis.
